values: Using and extending the island richness table
Regression data contains one spatial unit per row with species richness and matching land area.
Use island, n_spp and area_km2. log columns are formula-driven for log-log species-area models.
Append one row to the Excel table. Give a stable island_id, exact spatial unit, richness definition, area source URL and inclusion decision.
Area must describe the same island or archipelago covered by the richness count. Do not mix country area with main-island richness.
Use the same Scarabaeinae definition and treatment of native, endemic and introduced species across rows.
Yes is a working inclusion set. Review means resolve scope/comparability before fitting. No excludes unresolved records.
For future additions, use one consistent GIS product where possible: USGS Global Islands, DOI 10.5066/P91ZCSGM.
Australia, New Guinea and Madagascar can dominate the slope and differ biogeographically from oceanic islands. Fit sensitivity models with and without them.
New Zealand, New Caledonia and Guadeloupe are multi-island units. Include them only if richness was compiled for the same full unit.
Counts are exact row counts by the source Island label. The ambiguous Lesser Antilles record remains visible but excluded.
Rows marked Provisional should be replaced with values from the chosen canonical GIS dataset before final analysis.
Plot log richness versus log area; inspect leverage; compare oceanic-only, all-island and continental-fragment sensitivity models.
